title: Phase D review 3 — the chips and the terminal, built

steps.headline: Attached files are the design-C cards: a preview on top, the name in a strip along the bottom, ✕ always visible.
steps.changed: Markdown, text and code files show their first lines — markdown rendered properly (headings, bold, lists), never raw ##. Pictures show a thumbnail; everything else a big type glyph with the extension. The name strip is 12 px with a type icon.
steps.measured: 128 × 96 px cards vs 48 × 48 squares; the first 600 bytes of a file are read for the preview, never more than 4 KB
steps.notice: You can read what you attached and see inside text files before sending. The attachment row is twice as tall as before while files are attached. The same rendered-markdown rule now applies to file thumbnails in the session files pane, Deliverables and tool cards.
steps.risk: In these screenshots the PNG shows the glyph, not its picture — the screenshot tool cannot load local images; in the app a picture that fails to load falls back to the same glyph rather than a broken image.

steps.headline: Under a wallpaper theme the terminal now sits on the theme's panel colour at 80% — your pick — instead of 60% text straight over the picture.
steps.changed: A theme guarantee, not a setting: any theme with a wallpaper or gradient gets the panel backing at 80%; a pack asking for less is raised to 80%, one asking for more is honoured. Flat themes are byte-identical to before.
steps.measured: Panel colour at 80% opacity; flat themes unchanged
steps.notice: Terminal text reads like chat text does over wallpapers. Meadow Mist's own hand-made terminal backdrop now shows only faintly through the panel. Gradient themes get the same treatment.
steps.risk: The Terminal Opacity slider in the theme editor still goes below 80% on wallpaper themes, where it now does nothing — filed for a follow-up. The sample text is the workbench's frozen screen, not a live session. Flat themes are not shown here because they did not change at all — the deck refuses to ring a picture with no difference.
